conviction_note: The half-year numbers are already out: NAV per share of about 869p and GPV of about £1,695m were pre-released on 26 Oct, and the £50m post-period Revolut sale on 5 Nov. What is left for the release is the final NAV (it was revised up 5p last year), what the Board does with roughly £126m of pro forma cash (a capital-return upsize is possible but not signalled) and the outlook. abs_move is 4.0, above the 3% pre-released base, because results days on this 40%-vol name have moved -3.3%, +5.5% and +16.1% over the last three; p_up is 55 because the shares trade at a 28% discount after giving back the whole trading-update rally. Findings sum +0.7, the scaled number is +0.4, and both are small for the same reason: nothing decisive is unpublished.

already_public.what: HY27 trading update: NAV per share expected up 14% to c.869p (31 Mar 2026: 760p), GPV c.£1,695m, fair value uplift c.£244m (16%), realisations c.£109m (Revolut c.£71m, ICEYE c.£22m), group cash £76m, undrawn £60m RCF, £16m bought back in H1, £175m first close of the Growth Fund
Buyback extended by £10m, to be deployed once the existing £15m tranche is used up; 173,353,019 voting shares

Post-period partial Revolut realisation of c.£50m at the expected 30 Sep fair value (Revolut holding c.£130m at 30 Sep); FY27 realisations to date over £150m; notice of results on 24 Nov with an analyst presentation at 09:30 GMT
Capital allocation policy: at least 10% of realisation proceeds returned through buybacks

new_in_release.expect: Final 30 Sep NAV per share close to the c.869p estimate. Last year the estimate of 719p came out at 724p, a small upward revision. A small upward lean, with low confidence.

Molten pays no dividend. The capital-return line is the buyback: the 10% policy minimum on more than £150m of FY27 realisations is already covered by the £16m spent in H1 plus the £10m extension. An upsize or a new tranche is possible given c.£126m of pro forma cash, but nothing has signalled one. A small positive lean.

Post-period portfolio commentary (ICEYE, Isar, Revolut at the $115bn secondary) and outlook on exit markets and third-party funds. Unknown. This is where the June 2026 results-day move of +16% came from (the ICEYE round).
Molten gives no earnings guidance, and none is expected.

bar: NAV per share c.869p and GPV c.£1,695m, from the company's own HY27 trading update (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/eqs/molten-ventures--grow/half-year-trading-update/9840300). No sell-side consensus was found.
session_check: bmo. The issuer's 5 Nov 2026 RNS says it 'will announce its half year results on Tuesday 24 November 2026', with an analyst presentation at 09:30am GMT the same morning. Its prior results RNSs went out at 07:00 (HY27 trading update) and 08:04 BST (FY26 finals), so the window is the 23 Nov close to the 24 Nov close. Source: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/eqs/molten-ventures--grow/portfolio-update-and-notice-of-results/9859430
positioning_check: FCA aggregated net short position of 1.09%, position date 2026-11-04, re-read from https://www.fca.org.uk/publication/documents/aggregated-current-net-short-positions.csv on 2026-11-23. It was 1.01% before (+0.08pp, building slightly). This is small and not crowded, and it has not changed since before the 5 Nov drop.

findings.finding: The post-period £50m Revolut sale lifts FY27 realisations to more than £150m and pro forma group cash to about £126m (£76m at 30 Sep plus about £50m), plus a £60m undrawn RCF. The 10%-of-realisations buyback minimum is already met by the £16m spent in H1 and the £10m extension, so the interims are the Board's first chance to say what the Revolut cash buys. A further buyback upsize would be new; continued deployment would be neutral.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The +£10m buyback in Oct 2025 came with the HY26 trading update, not on results day. The 26 Oct 2026 extension shared a day with the trading update (+4.9%), so the buyback effect cannot be isolated.
findings.why_not_priced: The sale itself is priced: the stock fell 5.7% on 5 Nov and has drifted down since. What the money is used for is not announced. If the market expected a large new return, the discount would not have widened from about 19% to 28% since 27 Oct.
findings.independence: The FY26 results restate the policy minimum and that the Board's 'key focus' is narrowing the discount: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/eqs/molten-ventures--grow/final-results-for-the-year-ended-31-march-202-/9608559 (the same issuer, a different document).

findings.finding: At the 626.5p sealed spot the shares stand 27.9% below the company's own pre-released c.869p NAV. On the 27 Oct close of 709p the gap was 18.4%, and HL gives a 12-month average discount of 26%. GROW is down 10.6% over 20 sessions against -2.4% for the FTSE 250 and -2.2% for Chrysalis. The results confirm a NAV the market has already marked down to.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nov 2025 interims, also with NAV pre-released (719p estimate, 724p final): +5.5% on results day.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: it agrees with the run-up and with the +1.03 sealed lean, so it is mostly the free control. It is filed small because confirming the NAV removes estimate risk at a discount wider than the 12-month average.
findings.independence: The HL page shows an estimated NAV of 869p, a -22.5% discount on its own date and a 26% 12-month average: https://www.hl.co.uk/shares/shares-search-results/m/molten-ventures-plc-ordinary-shares-1p

outside_window.finding: Investor Meet Company retail presentation on Friday 27 Nov 2026, three days after the exit window.
Molten East and the dedicated Secondaries funds are 'on track for a first close by the end of FY27', which is after the window.

searched_and_found_nothing: No November 2026 broker preview or target price (Deutsche Numis, Berenberg) was found in search.
No post-30-Sep funding round or valuation event was found for ICEYE (last round: Series F at over €10bn, Jun 2026) or Isar Aerospace (Series D, Jun 2026, valuation undisclosed).
Ledger IPO: no S-1 or pricing news since the Jan-Apr 2026 reports.

Revolut: the $115bn secondary completed 4 Nov (https://buttondown.com/thesecondarybrief/archive/2026-11-05/). Molten sold at its Sep fair value the next day, so no hidden post-period uplift could be established.
lse.co.uk share-price news page returned no parseable headlines.
Sharecast, Proactive and Investors' Chronicle were not tried; the brief records them as 403 to both tools.

rejected_candidates.candidate: HY27 NAV per share up 14% to c.869p and GPV up 11% will be confirmed in the interims
rejected_candidates.detail: Already public since 26 Oct. Filed only as the bar and in already_public, and folded into finding 2's discount framing rather than counted as a second finding.

rejected_candidates.candidate: The Revolut $115bn secondary (4 Nov) implies a post-period uplift to Molten's remaining Revolut stake
rejected_candidates.detail: Molten's own 5 Nov RNS says the further c.£50m was realised at the expected 30 Sep fair value, so the Sep mark already sits at the transaction price.

baseline_tension: It agrees with the lean (+1.03, from a slightly building but small short and a negative run-up) and with the -10.6% 20-day run-up. Finding 2 is that same discount, so it was sized small; the only element independent of the price is the possible capital-return line.
language_note: Nothing the English sources did not already carry. The domestic RNS record on Investegate supplied the primary documents (the trading update, the buyback extension, the notice of results with the 09:30 presentation time, and the FY26 capital-allocation policy) that the wire summaries paraphrase. Domestic retail-platform pages (HL, AJ Bell) added only the discount history and last year's 719p-to-724p revision context.
lessons_applied: 'Positioning is the thing to beat, not the thing to agree with': the discount and run-up finding agrees with the sealed lean, so it went from +0.4 to +0.2.

'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0': no finding rests on the pre-released NAV or GPV. The capital-return finding was trimmed from +0.6 to +0.5 because the policy minimum is already met.

'Let the reaction history move p_up, not abs_move_pct' and the pre-released base of about 3%: abs_move kept at 4.0, not cut to 3, because this name's results days have moved -3.3%, +5.5% and +16.1%. p_up kept at 55, inside the 45-55 band for a pre-released period.
